title: The harvest (Revelation 14)
hookLine: blessed are the dead who die in the Lord; they rest from their labors
tomorrow: The song of Moses and the Lamb

lines: A FIELD READY TO BE CUT.
cards: A funeral on a gray afternoon. People in dark coats stand around an open grave. The minister opens a worn book and reads lines that sound older than everyone there: a voice from heaven, telling John to write.
Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord. They rest from their labors. And their works follow them.
Those words sit in the middle of Revelation fourteen, a chapter of flying angels, a sickle, and a field ready to be cut. Today's word is that field.

teach.h: THE LAMB STILL STANDS ON SION.
teach.b: First, a mountain. The Lamb stands on Mount Sion with his people, and they sing a new song no one else can learn. After yesterday's beasts, the Lamb is still standing.

Second, the voice: "Write, Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord from henceforth: Yea, saith the Spirit, that they may rest from their labours; and their works do follow them." Notice the order. Rest first.
Then their works follow, like a family walking behind a coffin. Nothing good they did is lost. The old Anglican Book of Common Prayer sets this verse in its burial service, read at the grave.

teach.h: THE SICKLE, AND A RIPE FIELD.
teach.b: John sees one "like unto the Son of man" on a white cloud with a sharp sickle, and an angel calls: "Thrust in thy sickle, and reap: for the time is come for thee to reap; for the harvest of the earth is ripe."
Jesus told stories like this: wheat and weeds growing together until the harvest. Here it comes.
A second harvest follows, grapes thrown into a winepress, a hard picture of judgment. Some readers take it literally; others hear picture language.
Fourth, for anyone who has buried someone who died in faith, the chapter says two things at once: those who die in the Lord are at rest, and their works are not left behind.
The harvest is when what was growing is finally gathered in.

how: Christians pray for or remember their dead at funerals and on days set aside for them, and Revelation 14:13 is read in some burial services; churches differ on praying for the dead, with Catholic and Orthodox Christians praying for them directly and some Protestants giving thanks for them instead.

games.q: you hear a voice from heaven speaking of those who have died in the Lord. what does it say comes first for them?
o: judgment for every labor they left undone.
rest from their labors, with their works following them.
a long wait with nothing to show for their lives.
games.why: the Spirit says they rest from their labors, and their works follow them. rest first, and the good they did goes with them.

practice: Let one person who has died come to mind, a grandparent, a friend, someone you never got to say goodbye to, and see their face.
Think of one good thing of theirs that still follows them: a recipe you still cook, a habit of kindness, a phrase you catch yourself saying.

If you pray, commend them to God by name and ask that they rest; if not, thank them silently. And if grief is heavy today, you don't have to carry it alone: call or text 988 in the US, or reach local emergency help.

wordCard.voice: The harvest. In Revelation fourteen, the field of the earth gathered in at the end, and the dead who die in the Lord at rest, with their works following them.

orig.note: Greek: harvest, reaping. the word for the ripe harvest of the earth in Revelation 14:15.
